definitions.explanation: The smallest unit of matter that retains the properties of an element. A fundamental concept in chemistry and physics.

examples.japanese: {原子|げんし}は{目|め}に{見|み}えない。
examples.english: Atoms are invisible to the eye.

examples.japanese: {水|みず}は{水素|すいそ}{原子|げんし}と{酸素|さんそ}{原子|げんし}からできている。
examples.english: Water is made of hydrogen atoms and oxygen atoms.

examples.japanese: {原子|げんし}{爆弾|ばくだん}は{原子|げんし}の{分裂|ぶんれつ}を{利用|りよう}する。
examples.english: Atomic bombs use the splitting of atoms.

notes:
{原子|げんし} is the smallest unit of a chemical element. Composed of {原|げん} (origin/fundamental) + {子|し} (small unit/particle).

COMPOUNDS:
- {原子|げんし}{爆弾|ばくだん} ({原爆|げんばく}): atomic bomb
- {原子|げんし}{力|りょく}: atomic/nuclear power
- {原子|げんし}{番号|ばんごう}: atomic number
- {原子|げんし}{核|かく}: atomic nucleus
- {原子|げんし}{力|りょく}{発電所|はつでんしょ} ({原発|げんぱつ}): nuclear power plant

RELATED PARTICLES:
- {分子|ぶんし}: molecule (group of atoms)
- {電子|でんし}: electron
- {陽子|ようし}: proton
- {中性子|ちゅうせいし}: neutron

WATCH OUT:
{原始|げんし} means "primitive" or "primeval" — a completely different word. See the cross-reference above.
